bull_bear.body: Prioritizing project launches and capex for high-return assets (Worli, Commerz III, Thane); no dividends paid; debt reduction secondary to growth; land acquisition via redevelopment and TDRs to minimize cash outflow.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Regulatory delays in Thane (Eco-Sensitive Zone reinstatement risk); interest rate volatility impacting buyer affordability; delays in redevelopment approvals; oversupply risk in non-premium segments; execution risk on large commercial projects.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, bullish, and proactive; management emphasizes pricing power, supply scarcity, and execution discipline; avoids overpromising on timelines but signals strong momentum; tone reflects control over narrative and market position.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Buyers are purchasing 2-3 units to create 12,000-15,000 sq.ft duplexes — indicating ultra-high-net-worth demand and asset consolidation behavior, not just housing needs; SRA redevelopment success without intermediaries is a rare competitive moat in Mumbai.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body: - Disciplined capital allocation with a focus on internal accruals and maintaining a strong balance sheet.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Brand reputation with higher recall that influences buying decisions and supports premium realizations
- Track record of quality project execution with contemporary architecture
- Continuous cash flows from investment/development properties, providing stability through adverse business cycles
- Conservative debt practice combined with a strong cash balance, giving significant leveraging headroom for expansion
- Outsourcing model using globally renowned architects/contractors, enabling scalability and contemporary design/construction quality
- Strong corporate governance culture with transparency and high business ethics
- Experienced, highly qualified design and project-management execution team
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Delays in project approvals — Management flags unanticipated delays in obtaining regulatory/project approvals as a challenge to executing its development pipeline on schedule.
- Skilled labour availability — Availability of an accomplished and trained labour force is flagged as a constraint on project execution.
- Rising manpower cost — Increased cost of manpower is cited as a cost pressure on project execution and margins.
- Construction cost inflation — Rising cost of construction, led by increases in commodity prices, is flagged as pressuring development economics.
- Dependence on auxiliary infrastructure growth — Company flags the pace of growth in auxiliary infrastructure facilities (roads, utilities, connectivity around project sites) as a factor affecting its developments.
- Regulatory burden — Management flags an over-regulated environment as a structural challenge to the real estate business.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Residential: 360 West (Worli) sold 77/200 units at ₹1.0-1.1 Cr/sq.ft RERA carpet; Goregaon/Borivali sold out Towers A/B; Mulund pricing up 5-10%; Retail: Borivali Mall pre-COVID consumption restored; Commercial: Commerz III nearing completion with strong tenant interest; Redevelopment: SRA site adjacent to Sky City cleared, 95% vacated.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Strengthen the development pipeline through strategic business development initiatives and acquisition of new land parcels
- Expand retail footprint through development of new retail destinations across strategic locations
- Expand presence in key markets while strengthening the portfolio across residential, commercial, retail and hospitality segments
- Grow development potential through a balanced mix of land acquisitions, redevelopment opportunities and strategic partnerships in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region
- Company pays dividends via quarterly interim payouts rather than a single final dividend; four interim dividends of Rs. 2 per equity share each (Rs. 8 aggregate) were declared for FY2025-26 and put to shareholders at the AGM to be confirmed as the final dividend for the year. It complies with the statutory requirement to transfer dividends and shares unclaimed for 7 consecutive years to the Investor Education Protection Fund (IEPF).
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY 2025-26 the Company launched Elysian Tower D at Oberoi Garden City, Goregaon East and Tower H at the Sky City project in Borivali East. Sky City (Borivali East, ~25 acre parcel, estimated total carpet area of about 4.5 million sq.ft.) received occupancy certificates for Tower A to E. Forestville at Kolshet, Thane is an under-development ~18 acre parcel with an estimated total carpet area of about 1.8 million sq.ft. Jardin, at Oberoi Garden City Thane (Pokhran Road-2), is an under-development ~75 acre parcel. Three Sixty West, Worli, a mixed-use residential development of 2 high-rise towers, was developed through a joint-venture entity; the Company retired as a member of that unincorporated association on March 3, 2023 and currently owns apartments in the project. On the business-development front, the Company added close to 4 million square feet of development potential during the year across key micro-markets in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, through a mix of land acquisitions, redevelopment opportunities and strategic partnerships, strengthening its future development pipeline.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Real estate sector benefiting from structural trends of rising urbanization, increasing disposable incomes and evolving consumer preferences
- Residential demand remains strong, especially in mid-income and premium segments, supported by stable interest rates and renewed buyer confidence
- Commercial real estate witnessing gradual recovery driven by demand for high-quality office space and growth in IT, BFSI and startup sectors
- Mumbai residential demand supported by a continued shift from rental to ownership housing and homebuyers prioritizing larger living spaces and improved amenities
- Grade A office leasing across metro cities strengthening, led by demand from global capability centres and domestic corporates and a shift toward world-class, sustainable infrastructure; Company's Commercial Offices at International Business Park operating at a record occupancy level of ~91%
- Retail demand for premium destinations continues to outmatch supply of spaces aligned with evolving occupier expectations; Retail Portfolio strengthening with addition of leading global brands across technology, entertainment, fashion and dining
- Infrastructure development (metro rail expansion, coastal road, trans-harbour connectivity) expected to be a key catalyst unlocking new growth corridors and positively impacting property values
- India's expanding affluent consumer base and growing billionaire population driving demand for premium, design-led and future-ready developments, with structural premiumisation favouring luxury and upper-tier residential segments
- Company added close to 4 million square feet of development potential during the year across key micro-markets in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, through a mix of land acquisitions, redevelopment opportunities and strategic partnerships
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers
